task1.title: Average carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions per person, 1967–2007
task1.prompt: The graph below shows average carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions per person in the United Kingdom, Sweden, Italy and Portugal between 1967 and 2007.

chartDesc.title: Average carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions per person, 1967–2007
chartDesc.overview: Over the 40-year period, average CO2 emissions per person decreased in the UK and Sweden, while increasing in Italy and Portugal. The UK had the highest emissions throughout the entire period, whereas Portugal started with the lowest but rose significantly.
keyFeatures: UK emissions declined gradually from nearly 11 metric tonnes (approx. 10.8) in 1967 to around 8.7 metric tonnes in 2007.
Sweden peaked at around 10.3 metric tonnes in 1977 before dropping sharply to roughly 5.4 metric tonnes by 2007.
Italy's emissions grew steadily from about 4.2 metric tonnes in 1967 to plateau at 7.7 metric tonnes in 1997 and 2007.
Portugal's emissions increased quadruply from approximately 1.2 metric tonnes in 1967 to around 5.4 metric tonnes in 2007, converging with Sweden's level by the end of the period.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Reasons for learning a foreign language
task2.prompt:
Some people say that the only reason for learning a foreign language is in order to travel to or work in a foreign country. Others say that these are not the only reasons why someone should learn a foreign language.

Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
